explanation: The metabolic pool contains compounds that can be dynamically routed to catabolic or anabolic pathways. Anabolism utilizes respiratory intermediates to build macromolecules: 1) Carbohydrates: synthesized starting with acetyl-CoA, effectively reversing glycolysis via alternative pathways. 2) Fats: synthesized by converting G3P into glycerol, and connecting acetyl groups in pairs to form fatty acid chains. 3) Proteins: assembled from combinations of 20 amino acids. While adult humans can synthesize 11 of these amino acids internally, the remaining 9 cannot be synthesized and are classified as essential amino acids, meaning they must be obtained through the diet.
